title: [Keyboard Manager] Bidirectional Alt/Win remapping causes both keys to trigger the Windows key

judgment.rationale: There is already a focused upstream fix attempt for this exact Alt/Win swap failure, and it should be followed instead of starting parallel design work in this batch.
evidence: The issue gives a concrete bidirectional Left Alt/Left Win swap repro on an Apple Magic Keyboard and explains the expected non-recursive behavior clearly.
Open draft PR #49748 explicitly states it is a candidate fix related to #49677.
That PR explains the recursion guard was treating physical events as injected when dwExtraInfo happened to share the Keyboard Manager flag bit.
The PR already includes a regression test and local validation, but it also states that validation on the reporter's Apple Magic Keyboard environment is still pending.
judgment.recommended_action: Track PR #49748 and retest on Apple Magic Keyboard hardware before closing the issue rather than opening competing Keyboard Manager work.

fix_assessment.rationale: An upstream fix attempt already targets this exact symptom, although confirmation on the reporter's hardware is still pending.

issue_context.summary: Bidirectional Alt/Win swapping on an Apple Magic Keyboard turns both physical keys into the Windows key. A draft upstream PR already targets this failure with a concrete recursion-guard fix and regression test.
known_information: The reporter is on PowerToys 0.100.2 and uses an Apple Magic Keyboard on Windows with a Korean setup.
The issue body clearly distinguishes expected swapped behavior from the actual behavior where both keys open Start / act as Win.
There are no public issue comments yet, but the upstream PR body explicitly marks itself as related to #49677.
PR #49748 says the exact reporter hardware validation is still pending even though the added regression test passes.
inferences: The issue is already actively investigated in code by another contributor, so new dashboard design work would be duplicative.
The remaining uncertainty is validation breadth on the reporter's exact hardware/input stack, not whether the issue deserves ownership.
issue_context.analysis: Because a scoped PR already exists and explains its theory of failure, the bounded dashboard action is to mark this handled by that PR. The batch should not fork a second design when the only missing piece is confirmation on the issue's exact Apple Magic Keyboard environment.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full issue body and confirmed the repro and expected behavior are already precise.
Reviewed draft PR #49748 in detail, including its root-cause explanation, test summary, and the explicit note that reporter-hardware validation is still pending.
Compared the PR scope with the issue symptom and confirmed it is not generic unrelated Keyboard Manager work.

author: propassionist

confidence.rationale: The PR is highly relevant, but its own description admits the reporter's exact hardware path is not fully confirmed yet.
